title: An Alfresco rule dispatching a typed APPROVE operation makes the approval a business event, not a file version
content:
The Alfresco demo uses a behaviour or rule bound to a content state change, dispatching a typed APPROVE operation into Powerhouse. The design choice being demonstrated is the separation itself: the approval is modelled as a business event with its own identity, rather than as a side effect of the document version that happened to carry it.

That framing exists because of the paired fit finding for the same seven partners — Alfresco records document events (versions, uploads, moves) and not the decision behind them. Emitting APPROVE as its own typed operation makes the decision addressable, replayable and attributable independently of the file's revision history, which is the property an approval workflow is actually audited on.

The cohort is seven Alfresco partners: BE, ES, two in DE plus one German multi-site, one Nordic (NO/SE/DK) and one DE with RO/IN delivery. Two are at "2 · next" and five at "3 · later", with no do-not-pitch entries. As with Odoo, the integration point is specific enough to be estimated without further research.
